caption:
Costa Rica spans less than 200 kilometres from the Caribbean to the Pacific across its narrowest corridor.

Between the two coasts, the mountain ranges climb from sea level to over 3,400 metres before dropping back down to the ocean. That geography compresses several distinct ecosystems into short drives, shifting from cool montane pastures to coastal valleys within a couple of hours.

High ridgelines on the Pacific slope catch rising moisture as the land heats up during the morning. By midday, clouds settle against the pasture hills before clearing back out toward evening.
